message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to cancel a date because I'm really tired. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I've been talking to this guy for two weeks. The first date went well, and we had a second date on Wednesday. Now it's Friday in Australia. On the second date, I mentioned that some things she said over the last week had been a bit overwhelming, but I wanted to be transparent. I told her it hasn't freaked me out, but I just wanted to take things slow, and she understood. We made plans to hang out on Friday night to watch a movie, which would have been our third date. This week has been really long for me. I had about four hours of sleep and worked from 7 am to 5 pm with only a half-hour break. He asked me around 5:30 pm if we were grabbing dinner or if he should get something himself. I told him I feel horrible but I'm absolutely shattered and would probably just fall asleep. I asked if we could do Sunday instead, and I said I'd take him out to lunch, I'd pay, and we could watch a movie. I haven't received a response yet. Now I'm worried that after me wanting to take things slow and then canceling the date, he might think I'm not interested anymore. I'm wondering if I'm being petty by rescheduling the date when he already has doubts about me. Hmm, so I need to consider a few things here. First, my well-being. I was extremely tired and didn't have the energy for a date. It's important to take care of myself. If I went out, I might have been irritable or not fully present, which isn't fair to either of us. On the other hand, communication is key in any relationship. I told him I was tired and asked to reschedule. I also offered to take him out on Sunday, which shows that I'm still interested but just need a break. Maybe he's considering whether I'm reliable or if I'm pulling away. I should also think about how he might perceive this. If I'm always canceling or rescheduling, it could send mixed signals. But in this case, it's just once, and I gave a valid reason. I also made an effort to reschedule, which is positive. I wonder if I should have communicated earlier about my exhaustion. Maybe if I had mentioned it before making plans, he would have understood better. But I did tell him on the spot, which is still good. Another point is that I offered to take him out on Sunday, which shows initiative and that I'm still interested. It might have been better to suggest a different time on Friday, but I was too tired. I'm also considering whether it's better to go out even when tired to show commitment. But I think it's more important to be genuine. If I force myself to go out when I'm not feeling well, it might lead to a bad experience for both of us. In conclusion, while it's important to communicate and be considerate of the other person's feelings, taking care of my own well-being is also crucial. Rescheduling once because I'm exhausted doesn't seem wrong, especially since I communicated clearly and offered to make it up. It might be a bit petty in the sense that it's a minor inconvenience, but overall, it's a reasonable decision.
